territorial_scope.description: Applies to transfers of personal data from Argentina to destinations without adequate legislation, and the model clauses bind importers established outside Argentine jurisdiction.

evidence.quote: el responsable del tratamiento radicado fuera de la jurisdicción argentina que reciba los datos personales

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Approves model contractual clauses for international transfers of personal data (assignment and services) to countries without adequate legislation. Controllers whose contracts depart from the models must seek DNPDP approval within 30 days of signing. Lists countries considered adequate. Adopted 16 Nov 2016.
summary.long: Approves two model contractual clauses for international transfers of personal data, one for assignment of data (Annex I) and one for provision of services by a processor (Annex II), to be used for transfers to countries without adequate legislation under Art. 12 of Law 25.326 and its regulatory decree. Art. 2 requires controllers that use contracts differing from the models, or lacking their principles and guarantees, to submit them to the DNPDP for approval within 30 days of signature. Art. 3 lists countries considered to have adequate legislation, including EU and EEA member states, Switzerland, Guernsey, Jersey, Isle of Man, Faroe Islands, Canada (private sector only), Andorra, New Zealand, Uruguay, and Israel (automated data only). The clauses give data subjects third-party beneficiary rights, require the importer to meet security, confidentiality and data-subject request duties, allow audits by the authority, and provide for suspension and termination of transfers where obligations are breached. The text sets no penalty amounts. It is dated 16 November 2016 and was published in the Boletín Oficial on 18 November 2016.

notes: Relations are the Ley 25.326 and Decreto 1558/01 legal bases plus EU reference materials cited only in the recitals. Art. 3 limits the listed adequate countries: Canada only for its private sector and Israel only for automatically processed data. The fetched text contains two model contracts (Anexo I for cesión, Anexo II for prestación de servicios), each followed by an Anexo A, and file numbers DI-2016-02874009 and DI-2016-02874003. Internal cross-reference inconsistencies: Anexo II cláusula 6 refers to 'epígrafe 1' and 'apartados 1 y 2' and to 'cláusula 3 o en la cláusula 10' although its paragraphs are lettered a) to c); Anexo I and II cláusula 4 i/5 j refer to 'punto 2' of a list that has no numbered points.

thresholds.note: No numeric cutoff changes legal treatment by scope, eligibility, exemption, tier, prohibition, benefit, penalty or price. The numbers present are procedural periods, coded as deadline events rather than thresholds: 30 calendar days to request approval (Art. 2), 10 calendar and 5 business days for responding to access and rectification requests (Annex II cl. 4 g), 5 business days to remedy non-compliance (cl. 5 d, Annex I; cl. 3 c, Annex II), and a 30-calendar-day suspension period that triggers contract resolution (cl. 8 b, Annex I; cl. 11 b, Annex II). The adequacy list in Art. 3 is a list of named jurisdictions, with partial scope limits (private sector only for Canada; automated data only for Israel), and contains no numeric cutoff.
